title: Curated brain pharmacology teaching catalog
scope: Sourced molecular identities and selected pharmacology with explicit model assumptions. No patient-specific PK, clinical effect or combination-safety prediction.

units.kiNM: nM; see evidenceType for assay Ki versus illustrative K*

modelAssumptions: Target affinities differ by assay, species, radioligand and receptor state. Ki, Kd, EC50 and IC50 are distinct.

Selected targets include assay-specific functional EC50/IC50 and response maxima, separate from binding Ki/Kd. Legacy efficacy coefficients and brainEquilibrationH remain illustrative. Bupropion brainPartition is rat-model-derived with estimated human transfer; other brainPartition values are illustrative.

Functional response curves retain experimental species, cell system, endpoint and reference response. Hill slopes, transfer to brain concentration and combination pooling are estimated unless explicitly sourced.
A measured cellular response is not a measured change in human neuron firing or cognition. Receptor reserve, signaling bias and anatomical context can change both magnitude and direction.
Default concentrations are demonstration exposures, not doses or therapeutic targets.

Selected CYP inhibition constants are measured in vitro; substrate-specific clearance fractions are derived from human AUC ratios under explicit assumptions. Liver exposure, parent-only inhibition and mixture transfer remain estimates. Missing quantitative evidence leaves interactions unmodeled.
Serotonergic interactions are qualitative, context-dependent and cannot be translated to a precise safety or symptom score.
Molecular conformers and structural identity do not validate network-level predictions.

occupancyCalibration.maximumEvidence: Fixed 100% maximum in the published model, not a fitted measurement
occupancyCalibration.concentrationBasis: Total-plasma-equivalent effect compartment; not free brain concentration
occupancyCalibration.equations: dCe/dt = ke0(Cp - Ce); occupancy = Ce / (EC50 + Ce); ng/mL = nM × molecularWeight / 1000
occupancyCalibration.context: N=18 healthy men after a single oral administration. EC50 and ke0 were estimated together using serial human PET and plasma data. The NeuroScope plasma compartment and virtual bolus are different from the published oral PK model.
limits: PET measures D2/3 radioligand displacement, whereas the app represents a combined D2 target. This is a striatal calibration, not an extrastriatal or whole-brain occupancy measurement.
The effect compartment is an empirical delay model. It does not identify blood–brain barrier permeability, a binding on/off rate, Kp,uu or a measured brain concentration.
The simulation transfers the published effect model to its simplified virtual plasma kinetics; route, absorption, patient variability and active metabolites are not reconstructed.
Competition with other compounds, altered endogenous drive, repeated exposure and links to functional neural responses are unvalidated transfers.
Parameter confidence intervals do not describe patient prediction intervals. Occupancy does not specify receptor activation or clinical response.

compounds.structureNote: 2D chemical record only; no inferred 3D cobalt coordination.

pathway.description: Cobalamins bind specific circulating carrier proteins. Transcobalamin presents bound vitamin to cellular uptake receptors. The displayed initial plasma amount is an annotation, not a predicted carrier partition.
Transcobalamin-bound cobalamin can bind the CD320 receptor and enter cells by receptor-mediated uptake. Brain delivery is regulated and cannot be inferred from the entered plasma level.
Internalization and lysosomal processing release cobalamin from its carrier. No endocytosis rate or neuronal accumulation is assigned in this model.
The MMACHC trafficking protein removes the cyano ligand from cyanocobalamin. Subsequent processing supplies methylcobalamin and adenosylcobalamin cofactor forms.

Active B12 cofactors support methionine synthase and methylmalonyl-CoA mutase pathways. This is a metabolic maintenance role, not an acute neurotransmitter receptor activation or a predicted repair response.

compounds.qualitativeExposureNote: The entered initial plasma concentration is recorded as an unevolved exposure annotation. Brain concentration, time-course, receptor occupancy and firing effects remain unknown, rather than zero.
